independence.note: This run used only public external sources plus the immediately prior clean_g1 cross_field checkpoint. No O, O-derived state, comparator/integrator output, or legacy pre_independence cross_field state was inspected.

search_bias: Continue outside mainstream agent literature, following quantitative mechanisms from control, operations research, distributed/runtime systems, and statistical debugging inward. This run started from the unresolved physical dual-control matched-baseline frontier, then branched to finite-budget allocation, semantics-aware checkpointing, negative-transfer-safe optimization, and sparse statistical diagnosis. Prefer real-system evidence, explicit cost/benefit surfaces, failure scopes, and mechanisms that can be transplanted without inheriting the source domain's assumptions.

checked_sources.source: Christian A. Larsson, Cristian R. Rojas, Xavier Bombois, Håkan Hjalmarsson, Experimental evaluation of model predictive control with excitation (MPC-X) on an industrial depropanizer, Journal of Process Control 31, 2015, DOI 10.1016/j.jprocont.2015.03.011
checked_sources.result: Real industrial depropanizer during normal operation. Degrading the controller model moved the reported performance measure p(theta) from nominal 0.0082 to 0.043; closed-loop re-identification with MPC-X restored acceptable performance in both simulator experiments and improved the real-plant experiment. The paper explicitly optimizes excitation around intended controller use rather than persistent excitation everywhere.

checked_sources.source: Zirui Cao et al., A budget-adaptive allocation rule for optimal computing budget allocation, European Journal of Operational Research 325(2), 2025, DOI 10.1016/j.ejor.2025.04.015; arXiv:2304.02377
checked_sources.result: Confirms the finite-budget versus asymptotic allocation distinction: T=O(k log k) budget-adaptive regime versus asymptotic OCBA recovered when T=omega(k log k). FAA/DAA discount hard-to-distinguish non-best designs under small budgets and converge toward OCBA as budget grows. Primary accessible text states significant small-budget improvements, but this run did not recover a clean exact percentage-point table from the primary full text, so no new numeric magnitude is asserted.

checked_sources.source: Tianyuan Wu, Chaokun Chang, Lunxi Cao, Wei Gao, Wei Wang, Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes, arXiv:2604.28138, 2026
checked_sources.result: OS-visible side-effect classification makes checkpointing sparse: more than 75% of turns have no recovery-relevant state; reported skip ratio reaches 87%. Recovery correctness rises from 8% chat-only to 100%; checkpoint traffic falls up to 87%; end-to-end execution stays within 1.9% of fault-free; restart-from-scratch adds up to 1.67x and every-turn full checkpointing up to 3.78x under dense co-location.

checked_sources.source: Ben Liblit, Cooperative Bug Isolation, UC Berkeley dissertation, 2004; project/dissertation materials
checked_sources.result: Sparse randomized predicate sampling reduced the bc case-study instrumentation overhead from about 13% without sampling to about 0.5% at 1/1000 sampling while preserving unbiased population-level evidence. Public deployment materials also report an important scale caveat: at 1/100 sampling, the then-current methods needed roughly 10,000-20,000 runs for accurate analysis.

checked_sources.source: Alice X. Zheng, Michael I. Jordan, Ben Liblit, Alex Aiken, Statistical Debugging of Sampled Programs, NeurIPS 2003; and related CBI case materials
checked_sources.result: Supports population-level statistical debugging from sparsely sampled user runs, using statistical ranking rather than complete traces. The useful transferable mechanism is unbiased sparse observability plus aggregation, not any claim that one sparse trace is sufficient.

checked_sources.source: Tinu Theckel Joy, Santu Rana, Sunil Gupta, Svetha Venkatesh, A flexible transfer learning framework for Bayesian optimization with convergence guarantee, Expert Systems with Applications 115, 2019
checked_sources.result: Models source observations as noisy target observations and estimates the source-target relatedness/noise from data; theoretical bounds improve over generic no-transfer BO and experiments span similar and mildly related tasks. No exact matched numeric effect was extracted in this run, so retained as mechanism evidence rather than a promoted quantitative candidate.

checked_sources.source: Michael Volpp et al., Meta-Learning Acquisition Functions for Transfer Learning in Bayesian Optimization, arXiv:1904.02642, 2019
checked_sources.result: Meta-learned acquisition functions are reported to fall back to general-acquisition performance when no exploitable structure is present. This is relevant to safe transfer, but the accessible abstract did not provide a numeric negative-transfer bound, so not promoted as a strong quantitative candidate.

candidates_new.mechanism: Application-oriented excitation: when an operational model becomes stale, choose interventions that maximize information specifically about model components that matter to downstream control quality, while enforcing operational constraints, instead of maximizing generic persistence/excitation.
candidates_new.primary_source: Larsson et al., Experimental evaluation of model predictive control with excitation (MPC-X) on an industrial depropanizer, Journal of Process Control 31 (2015), DOI 10.1016/j.jprocont.2015.03.011
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: On the depropanizer benchmark, a degraded controller model increased performance measure p(theta) from nominal 0.0082 to 0.043, deemed unacceptable. MPC-X closed-loop re-identification restored acceptable performance in both simulator experiments; on the real industrial plant, the reidentified model also improved performance under normal operation, though changing disturbances complicate a clean before/after application-cost comparison.
candidates_new.scope: Strong physical/industrial feasibility and performance-restoration evidence, but not a clean randomized matched comparison against passive-learning MPC on the real plant. Do not interpret 0.0082->0.043 as an effect size of MPC-X itself; it is the induced degradation that MPC-X then repairs. This candidate therefore answers the prior physical-feasibility branch more strongly than the exact passive-baseline-benefit branch.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: When a research system detects model/assumption drift, generate the cheapest targeted diagnostic interventions that discriminate only decision-relevant uncertainty, subject to safety/operational constraints. Avoid generic broad probing if the downstream decision depends on a much smaller parameter subspace.
candidates_new.confidence: high for real-system feasibility and scoped restoration; medium for transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Checkpoint only at state-changing semantic boundaries detected from observable side effects, choose checkpoint granularity from the changed state, and overlap checkpoint/restore work with naturally idle latency instead of checkpointing every logical turn.
candidates_new.primary_source: Wu et al., Crab: A Semantics-Aware Checkpoint/Restore Runtime for Agent Sandboxes, arXiv:2604.28138 (2026)
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: Across shell-intensive and code-repair workloads, more than 75% of turns produced no recovery-relevant state; one workload skipped checkpoints on 87% of turns. Recovery correctness improved from 8% for chat-only recovery to 100%; checkpoint traffic fell by up to 87%; execution with one injected crash per task stayed within 1.9% of fault-free time. Restart-from-scratch added up to 1.67x on SWE-Bench, while every-turn full checkpointing added up to 3.78x on Terminal-Bench at 96-sandbox density. Coordinator overhead was tens of microseconds per turn and asynchronous overlap kept exposed checkpoint delay near zero at median.
candidates_new.scope: 2026 preprint on agent sandboxes rather than a mature distributed-systems deployment; correctness and overhead depend on accurate classification of recovery-relevant OS effects. The transferable principle is side-effect-gated checkpointing and latency overlap, not the exact 87% skip rate.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For long-running research workflows, checkpoint after actions that materially alter recoverable external state or decision-critical durable state, skip read-only/redundant turns, use incremental/filesystem/full tiers according to effect scope, and schedule persistence during model/tool wait windows. This can simultaneously reduce checkpoint traffic and improve real recovery correctness compared with chat-only continuation.
candidates_new.confidence: high for reported benchmark results; medium-high for systems transfer

candidates_new.mechanism: Sparse randomized observability: instrument only a small unbiased random fraction of candidate diagnostic predicates/events per run, aggregate evidence across many independent runs, and use statistical ranking to localize failure causes instead of collecting complete traces from every execution.
primary_sources: Ben Liblit, Cooperative Bug Isolation, UC Berkeley PhD dissertation, 2004
Zheng, Jordan, Liblit, Aiken, Statistical Debugging of Sampled Programs, NeurIPS 2003
candidates_new.quantitative_evidence: In the bc case study, unconditional instrumentation cost about 13% overhead; randomized 1/1000 predicate sampling reduced overhead to about 0.5%. The deployment work also exposes the countervailing sample-complexity cost: at 1/100 sampling, the then-current analysis needed on the order of 10,000-20,000 runs for accurate statistical diagnosis.
candidates_new.scope: Software predicate instrumentation and population-scale deployed runs. Sparse sampling is not free: the method trades per-run observability cost for a larger number of independent runs and requires unbiased sampling plus enough aggregate data. It is a poor fit when failures are extremely rare and run volume is low unless sampling is adapted.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Instead of logging every internal signal on every research run, randomly sample a small subset of diagnostic signals while preserving known inclusion probabilities, then aggregate across repeated evaluations. This can make high-dimensional observability affordable, but the scheduler should raise sampling density for rare/high-value failures and explicitly track effective sample size.
candidates_new.confidence: high for original overhead tradeoff; medium-high for transfer

evidence_updates.update: Cao et al. 2025 directly supports the practical implementation path: FAA uses the known final budget as an anchor and DAA dynamically updates the anchor; both are fully sequential, budget-dependent, consistent, and converge back to asymptotic OCBA. Accessible primary text confirms significant small-budget improvement across small- and large-scale numerical experiments, but this run did not extract exact primary PCS percentage points, so the earlier finite-budget theorem/crossover remains the strongest quantitative anchor.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Physical dual-control experiment with exact matched passive/nominal quantitative identification-speed plus control-cost benefit
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: The industrial MPC-X depropanizer study supplies real-plant application-oriented excitation and performance restoration, but not a clean randomized passive-learning comparison under matched disturbances. The earlier laboratory adaptive dual MPC source similarly showed feasibility without a clean matched quantitative benefit.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: The exact frontier remains unresolved. Promote application-oriented active identification as a separate industrially validated mechanism, but do not claim the sought passive-baseline effect size was found.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Safe transfer optimization with guaranteed no-negative-transfer numerical fallback
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Joy et al. learn source-target relatedness as observation noise; Volpp et al. report fallback to generic acquisition performance when source structure is absent. These support the design principle of learned transfer strength/fallback, but the accessible primary materials in this run did not provide a clean matched quantitative negative-transfer detection threshold or cost.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Keep as promising mechanism evidence; do not promote without explicit quantitative target-only fallback performance or a theorem whose assumptions are operationally checkable.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Always-on complete telemetry for diagnosing research failures
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: CBI's bc case moved from roughly 13% overhead without sampling to roughly 0.5% with 1/1000 sampling, while retaining population-level statistical utility.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Reject complete instrumentation as a default. Use sparse unbiased telemetry when aggregate run volume is sufficient; retain targeted dense traces for rare failures or final confirmation.
